Fixed. The bug was in `onMutate`/`onError` of `useMarkShipped` (`modules/orders/orders.queries.ts`): it snapshotted and restored the *whole* orders array. With two ships in flight, each mutation's snapshot could be taken after the other's optimistic write had already landed — so when one failed, restoring its stale full-array snapshot silently wiped out the other row's still-in-flight (or already-succeeded) `shipped` status.

Changed the rollback to track only the failed row's prior status and patch just that one row back (`withStatus` helper), leaving every other row's cache entry untouched regardless of what else is concurrently in flight.

Added a regression test, `when one of two ships fails, only that row goes back` (`modules/orders/orders.queries.test.ts`), which ships two orders concurrently, resolves one and rejects the other, and asserts the successful row stays `shipped` while only the failed row reverts to `pending`.

`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm test` all exit 0 (27/27 tests pass). Done.
